coaching.title: Today's Run
coaching.message: Easy 8–10 miles, Z2 (130–140 bpm), rolling terrain if available but nothing steep. You ran 11.52 mi yesterday at 135 bpm—that's your second consecutive aerobic effort over 10 miles. In taper week 27, you're cutting volume but staying sharp; today is a flush run to promote blood flow and keep the aerobic base active without adding fatigue. Keep it conversational and sub-threshold. No intervals, no hill repeats.

coaching.title: Fuel Right
coaching.message: You logged 11.5 hours sleep last night—exceptional recovery. Use that to dial nutrition precisely: 100–120g carbs within 30 minutes of finishing today's run, paired with 20–25g protein (chocolate milk, rice + chicken, or a sports shake). You're in taper, so glycogen stores should be topped; don't under-fuel thinking you're resting. By race day (47 days out), your gut will need to handle 60–80g carbs/hour on the mountain. Train that now on longer efforts.

coaching.title: Recovery
coaching.message: Recovery score is 97/100 and resting HR is 62 bpm—your parasympathetic system is primed. Sleep quality was 96.4% efficiency; maintain that discipline: 10 p.m. bed, no screens after 9:30 p.m., cool dark room. In taper, sleep is a performance tool, not optional. You're 47 days from a 2,500m vert slog in thin air; compound sleep gains now into September. Aim for 8–9 hours every night through race week.

coaching.title: Mental Edge
coaching.message: You're exactly where you need to be: volume down, recovery metrics in the green, and specific work still in the bank. The Julian Alps 50K will test your ability to move smoothly on alpine singletrack when tired. Use these final 47 days to refine pacing discipline (not faster on easy days) and visualize the course—sparse aid stations mean self-sufficiency and rhythm matter more than pure fitness. Your aerobic base is built; execution is the variable now.
